title: Being Right About What You Meant
thesis: Clarified content can leave historical reliance reasonable while helping select the legitimate common condition under which an institution should repair the opportunity its inadequate guidance impaired.
contribution: An opportunity-sensitive account of public clarification that separates retention of an eligibility rule from duties governing its administration, gives a conditional further-opportunity verdict, and distinguishes content-invariant historical warrant from content-sensitive remedial baselines.
strongest_objection: The proposal may remain a useful application of familiar reliance duties without sufficient originality, and the threshold for an adequate further opportunity needs a defensible account of institutional purpose and competing claims.
originality_limitations: Bounded search only; no new foundational norm claimed; adjacent work on interpretation, reliance, annulment, metalinguistic negotiation and procedural fairness not comprehensively searched.
open_questions: How should adequate preparation opportunities be determined under severe constraints?
What baseline is justified when actual content remains unsettled?
Which institutional purposes can justify refusing otherwise feasible participation-preserving remedies?
Does adjacent literature already articulate the same differential role of content?
configuration_observation: No direct new model/effort/service-tier observation in resumed author context; coordinator fast-mode report not treated as runtime evidence.
